prompt: Which GST rate slabs apply in India after the 22 September 2025 reforms?
completion: Since 22 September 2025 (56th GST Council meeting) the main slabs are 5% (merit rate) and 18% (standard rate), plus a 40% special rate for sin and luxury goods. The 12% and 28% slabs were removed, and most items in them moved to 5% or 18%.

prompt: What is the GST rate on software development services?
completion: Software development services fall under SAC code 998314 and attract GST at 18% (CGST 9% + SGST 9% for intra-state, or IGST 18% for inter-state). ITC is available to the recipient if registered.

prompt: How do I file GSTR-3B?
completion:
To file GSTR-3B:
1. Log in to the GST portal (gst.gov.in).
2. Go to Returns > GSTR-3B and select the tax period.
3. Enter outward supplies (Table 3.1) and ITC claimed (Table 4).
4. Pay tax through the cash or credit ledger.
5. Submit and file using DSC or EVC.
Due date: 20th of the following month for monthly filers (22nd or 24th for QRMP filers, by state).

prompt: What are the due dates for GSTR-1?
completion: Monthly filers must file GSTR-1 by the 11th of the following month. QRMP quarterly filers must file by the 13th of the month after the quarter ends, and may upload invoices through IFF by the 13th of the first two months. QRMP is available to taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore.

prompt: Who must file GSTR-9 and what is its due date?
completion: GSTR-9 is the annual return, due by 31 December following the financial year. It is mandatory for taxpayers with aggregate turnover above ₹2 crore and optional up to ₹2 crore. Taxpayers with turnover above ₹5 crore must also file the GSTR-9C reconciliation statement.

prompt: Which businesses must issue e-invoices under GST?
completion: E-invoicing applies to registered businesses whose aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards, for B2B supplies, exports and supplies to SEZ. Taxpayers with turnover of ₹10 crore and above cannot report an invoice to the IRP more than 30 days after its date.

prompt: When is an e-way bill required for moving goods?
completion: An e-way bill is required when the consignment value exceeds ₹50,000. Part A holds invoice details and Part B the vehicle number, generated on the e-way bill portal. Validity is 1 day for every 200 km of distance for regular cargo.

prompt: What interest applies on late payment of GST?
completion: Interest under Section 50 is 18% per annum on tax paid late, counted from the day after the due date until the date of payment, and is charged on the net cash tax liability where ITC was available. For ITC wrongly availed and utilised, or excess reduction of output tax, the rate is 24% per annum.

prompt: What is the late fee for filing GSTR-3B after the due date?
completion: The default late fee is ₹50 per day (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST) for a return with tax liability, and ₹20 per day (₹10 + ₹10) for a nil return. It runs from the day after the due date until filing, subject to the maximum cap notified for the taxpayer's turnover band. Interest is charged separately.

prompt: In what order is input tax credit used to pay GST liability?
completion: IGST credit is used first against IGST, then CGST, then SGST/UTGST. CGST credit is used against CGST, then IGST, never against SGST. SGST/UTGST credit is used against SGST, then IGST, never against CGST. Only the balance after ITC is exhausted is paid in cash.

prompt: Which purchases are blocked from ITC under Section 17(5)?
completion: Section 17(5) blocks ITC on motor vehicles seating 13 or fewer persons, food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, club and fitness memberships, and construction of immovable property for own use (other than plant and machinery). Goods or services for personal use are also blocked. Exceptions apply where the supply is used for the same category of outward supply or is required by law.

prompt: Who can opt for the GST composition scheme and what are the rates?
completion: The composition scheme (Section 10) is for taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to ₹1.5 crore. Rates on turnover: 1% for manufacturers and traders (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST), 5% for restaurants not serving alcohol, and 6% for service providers under Section 10(2A) up to ₹50 lakh. Composition taxpayers cannot collect tax from customers, claim ITC or make inter-state outward supplies.

prompt: GSTR-3B भरने की अंतिम तारीख क्या है?
completion: मासिक रिटर्न भरने वाले करदाताओं के लिए GSTR-3B की अंतिम तारीख अगले महीने की 20 तारीख है। QRMP योजना वाले तिमाही करदाताओं के लिए यह तारीख राज्य के अनुसार अगले महीने की 22 या 24 तारीख होती है। देर से भरने पर लेट फीस और बकाया टैक्स पर 18% वार्षिक ब्याज लगता है।

prompt: What are the PF contribution rates for employee and employer?
completion: The employee contributes 12% of PF wages to EPF. The employer also pays 12%, split as 8.33% to the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) and 3.67% to EPF. EPS is calculated only up to the statutory wage ceiling. The employer additionally pays EPF administration charges and the EDLI contribution.

prompt: PF की वेतन सीमा कितनी है और यह कब बदली?
completion: 17 सितंबर 2026 से EPFO की वैधानिक वेतन सीमा ₹15,000 से बढ़ाकर ₹25,000 प्रति माह कर दी गई है। यह सीमा लगभग 12 साल बाद बदली है। अनिवार्य PF कवरेज और पेंशन (EPS) की गणना इसी सीमा तक होती है। इससे ऊँचे वेतन पर योगदान नियोक्ता की सहमति से किया जा सकता है।

prompt: ESI में कर्मचारी और नियोक्ता का योगदान कितना होता है?
completion: ESI में कर्मचारी कुल वेतन का 0.75% और नियोक्ता 3.25% योगदान देता है, यानी कुल 4%। ESI उन कर्मचारियों पर लागू होता है जिनका सकल वेतन ₹21,000 प्रति माह तक है (दिव्यांग कर्मचारियों के लिए ₹25,000)।

prompt: Is an employee with gross wages of ₹23,000 per month covered under ESI?
completion: No. ESI applies when gross wages are ₹21,000 per month or less (₹25,000 for persons with disabilities), so ₹23,000 is above the ceiling. An employee already covered stays covered until the end of the contribution period (April-September or October-March) in which wages crossed the ceiling.

prompt: What are the new tax regime slabs for salaried employees for FY 2025-26?
completion: Under the default new regime: up to ₹4 lakh nil; ₹4-8 lakh 5%; ₹8-12 lakh 10%; ₹12-16 lakh 15%; ₹16-20 lakh 20%; ₹20-24 lakh 25%; above ₹24 lakh 30%. Salaried taxpayers get a standard deduction of ₹75,000. Employers deduct TDS on salary on this basis unless the employee opts for the old regime.

prompt: Up to what salary is there no income tax under the new regime in FY 2025-26?
completion: Taxable income up to ₹12 lakh gets a full rebate under Section 87A (up to ₹60,000), so a salaried employee with gross salary up to ₹12.75 lakh pays no tax after the ₹75,000 standard deduction. The rebate does not apply to special-rate income such as capital gains under Sections 111A and 112A.

prompt: What is Form 16 and when must the employer issue it?
completion: Form 16 is the TDS certificate for salary under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Part A shows TDS deducted and deposited (generated from TRACES) and Part B shows the salary breakup, exemptions, deductions and tax computation. It must be issued by 15 June after the end of the financial year.

prompt: What are the due dates for filing Form 24Q?
completion: Form 24Q (quarterly TDS return on salary) is due 31 July for Q1 (April-June), 31 October for Q2, 31 January for Q3 and 31 May for Q4 (January-March). The Q4 return also carries the annual salary details used for Form 16 Part B. This applies to FY 2025-26 and earlier under the 1961 Act.

prompt: What changed for salary TDS under the Income-tax Act, 2025?
completion: The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026. TDS on salary moves from Section 192 to Section 392, the salary TDS certificate Form 16 becomes Form 130, and the quarterly return Form 24Q becomes Form 138. Compliance for FY 2025-26 still uses the old section numbers and forms.

prompt: How is gratuity calculated for 8 years of service with last drawn wages of ₹40,000?
completion: Gratuity = last drawn wages × 15/26 × completed years of service. Here: ₹40,000 × 15/26 × 8 = ₹1,84,615 (rounded). It is payable after 5 years of continuous service (1 year for fixed-term employees). The tax-exempt amount is the lowest of the formula amount, the gratuity actually paid and ₹20 lakh.

prompt: Who is eligible for statutory bonus and what percentage is payable?
completion: An employee drawing wages up to ₹21,000 per month who has worked at least 30 days in the year is eligible. The employer pays a minimum of 8.33% and a maximum of 20% of wages, calculated on wages subject to the ceiling notified under the Code on Wages, 2019.

prompt: What is professional tax and what is the maximum amount per year?
completion: Professional tax is a state-level tax on salaried people and professionals, deducted by the employer from salary and paid to the state government. The constitutional cap is ₹2,500 per person per year. Rates and slabs differ by state, and some states such as Delhi and Uttar Pradesh do not levy it.

prompt: What is the difference between GSTR-2A and GSTR-2B?
completion: GSTR-2A is a dynamic auto-drafted statement that keeps changing as suppliers file or amend their returns. GSTR-2B is a static statement generated for each month, around the 14th of the next month, from supplier filings up to the cut-off date. ITC in GSTR-3B is claimed as per GSTR-2B, so reconciliation is done against 2B.

prompt: How do I reconcile my purchase register with GSTR-2B?
completion:
Steps:
1. Download GSTR-2B (Excel or JSON) for the month.
2. Export the purchase register with supplier GSTIN, invoice number, date, taxable value and tax.
3. Match on GSTIN + invoice number + date after normalising invoice numbers.
4. Compare taxable value and CGST/SGST/IGST within a small rounding tolerance.
5. Classify as matched, value mismatch, in books only, or in 2B only.
6. Claim ITC on matched invoices and follow up with suppliers on the rest.

prompt: Why is a vendor invoice missing from my GSTR-2B?
completion: Common reasons: the supplier has not filed GSTR-1 or IFF for that period, the invoice was reported with a wrong recipient GSTIN, the invoice date falls in a different period, or the supplier filed after the 2B cut-off. Under Section 16(2)(aa) ITC is allowed only when the invoice is reflected in your GSTR-2B, so follow up with the supplier and claim in the month it appears.

prompt: What is an IRN in e-invoicing and how is it generated?
completion: The Invoice Reference Number (IRN) is a unique 64-character hash generated by the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) when you upload the invoice JSON. It is derived from the supplier GSTIN, financial year, document type and invoice number. The IRP returns it with a digitally signed QR code that must be printed on the invoice.

prompt: Can I cancel an e-invoice after generating the IRN?
completion: An IRN can be cancelled on the IRP only within 24 hours of generation. If an e-way bill exists against it, cancel the e-way bill first. After 24 hours the IRN cannot be cancelled on the IRP, so correct the transaction by issuing a credit note.

prompt: What details must a GST tax invoice contain?
completion: A tax invoice must show the supplier's name, address and GSTIN; a unique invoice number of up to 16 characters; the date of issue; the recipient's name, address and GSTIN if registered; HSN or SAC code; description, quantity and value; taxable value after discount; GST rate and amount (CGST, SGST, IGST); place of supply for inter-state sales; and the supplier's signature.

prompt: Within how many days must a service invoice be issued under GST?
completion: A tax invoice for services must be issued within 30 days from the date of supply of service. For insurers, banking companies and financial institutions including NBFCs the limit is 45 days. For goods, the invoice is issued at or before removal or delivery of the goods.

prompt: When can a supplier issue a GST credit note and what is the deadline?
completion: Under Section 34 a credit note is issued when the taxable value or tax charged exceeds what is payable, goods are returned, or services are found deficient. It is reported in GSTR-1, and the supplier can reduce output tax only if it is issued by 30 November following the financial year end or the annual return date, whichever is earlier. The recipient must reverse the matching ITC.

prompt: What is a GST debit note and who issues it?
completion: A debit note is issued by the supplier when the taxable value or tax charged in the original invoice is less than what is payable, for example after a price increase or undercharged tax. It carries the same particulars as an invoice, is reported in GSTR-1, increases the supplier's output tax and lets the recipient claim additional ITC as shown in GSTR-2B.

prompt: GSTR-2B के आधार पर ITC कैसे क्लेम करें?
completion: ITC केवल उसी इनवॉइस पर क्लेम होता है जो आपके GSTR-2B में दिखता है। पहले अपने खरीद रजिस्टर को GSTR-2B से मिलाएं, फिर मिलान वाले इनवॉइस का ITC GSTR-3B की टेबल 4 में दर्ज करें। जो इनवॉइस 2B में नहीं दिख रहे, उनके लिए सप्लायर से GSTR-1 फाइल करवाएं और अगले महीने क्लेम करें।

prompt: What is three-way matching in invoice processing?
completion: Three-way matching compares the purchase order (PO), the goods receipt note (GRN) and the vendor invoice before payment. Item, quantity and rate must agree within the set tolerance. If they differ, the invoice is put on hold for correction or a debit note, which prevents overpayment and wrong ITC claims.

prompt: What happens to ITC if I do not pay the supplier within 180 days?
completion: Under the second proviso to Section 16(2) and Rule 37, if the supplier is not paid within 180 days from the invoice date, the ITC availed must be reversed with interest at 18% per annum from the date of availing to the date of reversal. The ITC can be re-claimed once the payment is made.

prompt: What is the journal entry for a purchase of ₹1,00,000 with 18% GST within the same state?
completion: Dr Purchases ₹1,00,000; Dr Input CGST ₹9,000; Dr Input SGST ₹9,000; Cr Vendor (Sundry Creditor) ₹1,18,000. CGST and SGST are 9% each of the taxable value. Input CGST and SGST are asset ledgers used later to set off output tax.

prompt: What is the journal entry for an inter-state sale of ₹50,000 with 18% GST?
completion: Dr Customer (Sundry Debtor) ₹59,000; Cr Sales ₹50,000; Cr Output IGST ₹9,000. IGST is 18% of ₹50,000. Output IGST is a liability and is set off against Input IGST, then CGST, then SGST before any cash payment.

prompt: What are the advance tax due dates and percentages?
completion: Advance tax is due on 15 June (15% of the tax), 15 September (45% cumulative), 15 December (75% cumulative) and 15 March (100% cumulative). It applies if the net tax liability for the year is ₹10,000 or more. Taxpayers under the presumptive scheme can pay the full amount in one instalment by 15 March.

prompt: What are the due dates for AOC-4 and MGT-7 after an AGM?
completion: Form AOC-4 (financial statements) is due within 30 days of the AGM and Form MGT-7 (annual return) within 60 days of the AGM. For a 31 March year end the AGM must be held by 30 September, so AOC-4 is due by 30 October and MGT-7 by 29 November.

prompt: Within what time must a company hold its AGM?
completion: Under Section 96 of the Companies Act, 2013 a company must hold its AGM within six months from the end of the financial year, so by 30 September for a 31 March year end. The gap between two AGMs cannot exceed 15 months. The first AGM must be held within nine months of the first financial year end.

prompt: What master data must be set up in an ERP before posting GST invoices?
completion: Party masters with GSTIN, state and registration type; item or service masters with HSN/SAC code and GST rate; CGST, SGST and IGST ledgers for both input and output; the company's own GSTIN and state; and place-of-supply defaults. Without these the ERP cannot choose CGST/SGST or IGST correctly or prepare GST returns.

prompt: How does an ERP decide whether to charge CGST plus SGST or IGST?
completion: The ERP compares the supplier's location with the place of supply. If both are in the same state or union territory it applies CGST + SGST (or UTGST), each at half the rate. If they are in different states, or the supply is an import or export, it applies IGST at the full rate (exports are zero-rated).

prompt: What is a trial balance and what does it prove?
completion: A trial balance lists the closing debit and credit balances of all ledger accounts on a date. Total debits must equal total credits, which shows the books are arithmetically consistent. It does not prove accuracy: errors of omission, wrong account posting and compensating errors can still exist.

prompt: How do I prepare a bank reconciliation statement?
completion: Match every cash book entry to the bank statement. Entries in the books but not in the bank are timing items: cheques issued but not yet presented and cheques deposited but not yet cleared. Entries in the bank but not in the books, such as interest, charges and direct debits, must be booked. After adjustments the cash book balance agrees with the bank statement balance adjusted for the timing items.
